central_reading: Bernardo Kastrup has developed 'analytic idealism' as a systematic, empirically-informed idealist ontology. He argues that phenomenal consciousness is the sole ontological primitive, and that all physical structures — including the brain — exist solely as appearances (phenomenality) within consciousness. Neural correlates of consciousness are therefore correlates of dissociative processes within consciousness, not evidence that the brain produces consciousness.

argument_edges.relation_rationale: Direct peer-reviewed argument that all physical structure is circumscribed by consciousness, that brain-dependence does not refute idealism, and that NCCs are not evidence of production.

Provides the dissociation model that explains how brains can be correlates of consciousness without producing it — they are extrinsic appearances of dissociative processes within universal consciousness.
Argues that mind has epistemic and ontological primacy over matter, establishing the framework within which the brain-as-appearance thesis operates.
Summarizes the core reduction claim of analytic idealism: brain function is a pattern of consciousness excitation, not a cause of consciousness.
Provides a complementary idealist framework from a different philosophical tradition (perennial/contemplative), but currently unpublished in a peer-reviewed venue.
